why_this_file_exists: MATCHING-GOLDEN-2026-09-02.json is a DATED ARTIFACT and is never rewritten. But an adjudication can be wrong, and the commonest way for it to be wrong is that it recorded the world as it was on the day of capture rather than the answer that was always true: a market with no correct event, versus a market whose correct event our own bug hid from us. Correcting that by hand-editing tests/fixtures/matching_golden_inputs.json would work exactly once — capture_matching_golden_fixture.py re-derives correct_event_id straight from the artifact, so the next re-capture would silently revert it and the ratchet would cry regression all over again with nobody able to see why. So corrections live HERE, as data, with their evidence, and the capture script applies them. Every amendment is a claim about truth that a reader can check.
rules: An amendment names the market, what the artifact said, what it should say, and WHY — with evidence that can be re-run, not an assertion.

It is applied BEFORE the pair is built, so search_surfaced_the_answer and the adjudicated-event-must-be-present guarantee are both recomputed against the corrected answer rather than patched afterwards.

`was` is asserted against the artifact. If the artifact does not say what the amendment claims it says, the capture FAILS rather than applying a correction to a pair that has already moved underneath it.

An amendment never turns a FAILING pair green by itself. It changes the adjudicated answer; the baseline is then re-recorded and the ratchet reports the movement in whichever direction it really went.
Amendments are append-only. Superseding one means adding another that names it.
